title: Infinite q-log-convexity conjecture for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials
statement: For each $n\geq 1$, let $P_n(x)=\sum_k P_{n,k}x^k$, where $P_{n,k}$ is the number of permutations of $[n]=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ whose longest increasing subsequence has length $k$. A polynomial sequence is **infinitely q-log-convex** when every iterate of the relevant $q$-log-convexity operator is $q$-log-convex. **Infinite $q$-log-convexity conjecture.** The polynomial sequence $\{P_n(x)\}$ is infinitely $q$-log-convex. This proposes an iterated $q$-analogue of log-convexity for longest-increasing-subsequence polynomials; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
source_name: William Y. C. Chen, “Log-concavity and q-Log-convexity Conjectures on the Longest Increasing Subsequences of Permutations”, arXiv:0806.3392 (2008).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3392

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2008).
